A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the nineteenth century the household and family structures of Chile's lower class were in transition, with the household becoming increasingly nuclear and the family becoming increasingly extended.
, as the market economy expanded, the household became a less important unit of economic production.
the family was the basic social and economic unit in the rural areas of nineteenth-century Chile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the household is a flexible institution, it can be used by the state to maintain the existing social order.
the household structure of a particular class is not static but is subject to change.
, in the case of Chile, the transformation of agriculture from subsistence to commercialization was accompanied by a transformation in household structure from the stem family to the nuclear family.
